fit: observer-rated clinical signs and psychotropic dispensing in nursing homes
assessment: The nursing-home cohort uses caregiver or staff observation of visual hallucinations within a set of Lewy body features. It relates clinical signs to medications and diagnosis, without a timed meal or fig comparison.

fit: prospective older spinal-surgery cohort and postoperative delirium
assessment: The analysis includes 104 older people undergoing spinal surgery. It measures postoperative delirium and baseline Parkinson-related nonmotor features. Visual hallucinations are discussed in differentiating syndromes and are not counted against an edible exposure.

fit: mild cognitive impairment diagnostic groups and dopamine-transporter imaging
assessment: Clinical features and imaging characterize 75 participants with mild cognitive impairment across Lewy body and Alzheimer categories. The visual features are part of clinical classification. The original provides no study of visual episode frequency after dried fig ingestion.

fit: recurrent formed visual symptom definition and cortical perfusion
assessment: The study defines clinical presence using formed recurrent images and compares perfusion, metabolism and tau imaging. Meeting an occurrence criterion is distinct from counting visual episodes over time after an ingredient.

fit: clinical psychosis measures and quantitative brain susceptibility imaging
assessment: The recruited groups include Parkinson with and without dementia and healthy comparison subjects. Psychosis rating and iron imaging are clinical context. No independent dried fig exposure and visual episode response are observed.

fit: subcutaneous apomorphine case series and medication-linked visual symptoms
assessment: Table 1 records visual hallucinations before treatment in eight of twelve Parkinson patients. One later entry describes reduced but persistent visual hallucinations. The remaining entries do not describe persistent visual symptoms, and one patient with baseline complex hallucinations stopped because of falls. The mixed regimen and uncontrolled follow-up cannot isolate the drug or a fig effect.

fit: 125-person apomorphine cohort and visual symptom trajectories
assessment: Of 38 with active visual hallucinations at treatment start, fourteen improved markedly, nine improved to some extent, three worsened and twelve lacked a follow-up outcome. Other dopaminergic, antipsychotic and cholinesterase inhibitor therapy changed. The assessment is qualitative and not paired to food intake.

fit: apomorphine cognitive cohort and post-discharge worsening
assessment: The original reports 32 of 45 with active visual hallucinations at baseline and no new or worsened symptoms during inpatient titration. Nine worsened after discharge, including five whose hallucinations later resolved after treatment of intercurrent infection. Recruitment site and periods overlap the 125-person cohort, and shared patients are unverified.

fit: separate French Lewy body stimulation pilot and free recall
assessment: The French six-person NCT01340001 trial compared three-month active and sham conditions with free recall as the primary outcome. It supplies no separate visual episode-frequency contrast after food and is a separate study from the UK NCT02263937 trial.
